corrected_content.problem: Find the line integral of the function $f(x,y,z) = x^2+y-z,$ traversed along the line segment from $(0,1,-3)$ to $(-1,2,-2)?$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C f(x,y,z) \, \textrm{d}s  =  \int\limits_{t_a}^{t_b}  f(\mathbf r(t)) \, \| \mathbf r'(t) \| \, \textrm{d}t,
$$

 

where $C$ is the line segment from $(0,1,-3)$ to $(-1,2,-2).$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $\mathbf{a}=\mathbf{j}-3\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{b}=-\,\mathbf{i}+2\,\mathbf{j}-2\,\mathbf{k}.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{r}(t) & =\mathbf{a}+t\hspace{0.167em}(\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}) \\  & =(\mathbf{j}-3\mathbf{k})+t[(-\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}-2\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k})-(\mathbf{j}-3\mathbf{k})] \\  & =(\mathbf{j}-3\mathbf{k})+t(-\mathbf{i}+\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}) \\  & =-t\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+(t+1)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+(t-3)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}\end{aligned}
$$

where $0 \le t \le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x=-t, y=t+1,$ and $z=t-3$ along the segment.

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t)$ and $\| \mathbf{r}'(t) \|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t)\mathbf{i}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\mathbf{j}+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-3)\mathbf{k} \\  & =-\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k} \\ ‖{\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\right)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y,z) = x^2+y-z$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\mathbf{r}(t)) & =(-t)^{2}+(t+1)-(t-3) \\  & ={t}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y,z)\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(\mathbf{r}(t))\hspace{0.167em}‖{\mathbf{r}}^{'}(t)‖\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}+4)\cdot \sqrt{3}\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}+4)\hspace{0.167em}\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
